title: Audit finite-sample split likelihood-ratio coverage in a Bernoulli model
statement: Specialize universal inference to iid Bernoulli(p), a prespecified split of 20 observations into two groups of 10, training estimator q=(K1+1)/12, and alpha=1/20. Reproduce the all-p coverage proof and exact rejection probabilities on p in {1/10,...,9/10}.
source_locator: SRC-FORMAL-003, Section 2, Theorem 1; finite parameters chosen for calibration
status_basis: The guarantee follows from the published theorem under its assumptions. The finite Bernoulli benchmark is a curator-selected reproduction protocol; no calculation has been run.
plain_summary: Train a probability estimate on one half of a small coin-flip sample and evaluate it on the other half. Check that the resulting confidence set covers the true probability at the promised rate, without replacing exact evidence by simulation.
assumptions: Y1,...,Y20 are iid Bernoulli(p), with p in [0,1].
The first ten observations form D1 and the remaining ten form D0; the split is fixed before data are seen.
K1 and K0 are their respective success counts.
Use q=(K1+1)/12 and alpha=1/20; do not optimize either using the holdout data.
The ratio on the true distribution's support is well-defined; define endpoint confidence-set behavior explicitly.

Use the Bernoulli likelihood convention 0^0=1. Set the likelihood ratio to +infinity if its denominator is zero; the smoothed training estimator makes the numerator strictly positive. Retain T<=20 and reject only T>20.
scope: Reproduce a known guarantee and create a small exact benchmark. The selected sample size, smoothing rule and evaluation grid are curator choices. No claim of an optimal test, new interval or real-world model adequacy is included.
target: Prove P_p(p in C)>=19/20 for every p in [0,1], where C={theta: q^K0(1-q)^(10-K0)/[theta^K0(1-theta)^(10-K0)] <=20}; report exact rejection probabilities for nine specified rational p values.
success_criteria: Give the all-p coverage argument with independence and conditioning explicit.
Enumerate the 121 pairs (K1,K0) for each grid value using exact arithmetic and exact strict comparison T>20.
Report rational probabilities with a reproducible independent checker.
Treat endpoint p=0 and p=1 separately rather than silently dividing by zero.
Retain this as a calibration result, even if the AI completes it.
known_results: Universal Inference, Theorem 1, provides the finite-sample guarantee.
The SAVI review places this construction among e-value and e-process methods; fixed-split validity is not unrestricted optional-stopping validity.
significance: Tests the project's ability to distinguish theorem validity, numerical auditing and assumptions about data generation. It can reveal leakage and threshold-convention mistakes before harder statistical research.

requirements.data: No observed data required. The finite outcome space is specified mathematically.
requirements.compute: Small finite enumeration over 121 count pairs at each of nine rational parameter values. Rational bit sizes should be logged; wall time, memory and cost have not been measured.
requirements.theoretical_assumptions: iid Bernoulli sampling and a prespecified independent holdout split. The theorem's validity does not establish that actual observations obey this model.

ai_assessment.rationale: The proof and exact finite audit provide two complementary checks with limited implementation scope. The relevant capability is disciplined conditioning and exact arithmetic, not confidence asserted by a model.

clarity.reason: Data model, estimator, threshold, finite grid and endpoint cases are fixed.

decomposability.reason: Separate proof, count-pair probabilities, rejection decision and table audit.

methods.reason: A primary theorem and a later survey supply the needed framework.

search_or_symbolic.reason: Exact arithmetic and symbolic probability are directly useful.

checkability.reason: Each finite result has a short rational certificate and a separate general proof.

expertise.reason: A statistician should review leakage, support and coverage arguments.

significance.reason: Calibration has methodological value; there is no novelty claim.

verification_difficulty.reason: Small enumeration is easy, but it cannot replace the proof for all p.

ai_assessment.uncertainty: No implementation, empirical success rate or model comparison exists. A later protocol change, especially repeated split selection, may invalidate the reference guarantee.
ai_assessment.model_scope: No named model evaluated; assumes tool-using AI capable of elementary probability proofs and exact-arithmetic programming.

obstacles: Reusing holdout data to choose q breaks the conditioning argument.
Floating-point comparisons near T=20 can misclassify outcomes.
Checking nine values of p is not an all-p coverage proof.
Returning an interval hull is different from returning the exact confidence set.

steps: Derive the conditional expectation bound at the true parameter.
Verify the sample-count mass formula using binomial coefficients independently.
Use exact rational arithmetic to compare the test statistic with 20.
Sum rejection masses separately for each specified p and cross-check with a second implementation or manual cases.
Review the p=0 and p=1 support cases and document the confidence-set endpoint convention.
validation.human_review_difficulty: Moderate; probability review is necessary despite a small program.
validation.statement_alignment: Report a fixed-sample guarantee under iid sampling. Do not claim optional-stopping safety or empirical coverage in an unspecified real dataset.

known_attempts: Published universal-inference theorem; no project code, simulations or model attempt have been run.
unresolved_checks: An independent reviewer should confirm whether the benchmark's reproduction depth is sufficient before attempting power optimization.
Any extension to repeated splits, dependence or misspecification requires a separate problem record and proof.
